- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce peak forecasts by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is rising, cap upward momentum at 1–2% above recent mean to prevent false optimism.  
- After a sharp spike in price, model often overshoots — reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 periods to correct for momentum decay.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.3–0.7) and forecast diverges from recent 5-day average, align forecast to 5-day moving average to reduce noise.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome shows mean reversion toward 65–70 range after 10+ periods, adjust forecast downward by 2–4% per period to reflect diminishing volatility.  
- When sentiment is consistently high but price declines, model often fails to adjust — add a 1–2% downward bias to forecast to account for sentiment decay.
